quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: In the District of Columbia, is it illegal to turn left on a red light when traveling on a one-way street to another one-way street?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: In the District of Columbia, you cannot turn left on a red light. You can only turn right on a red light where it is allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This circular sign warns drivers about a railroad crossing ahead. Watch for trains when you see this sign.

questions.question: If you had an argument and feel angry, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you don't think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive fast on the highway to feel better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Anger affects your ability to drive safely. You need to be calm and focused on driving. Take time to cool down before you get behind the wheel.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children off, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the children to wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the road.
Speed up.
Turn on your emergency lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops with its lights flashing, watch carefully for children crossing or walking near the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are near a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to tell drivers to slow down and be careful. Watch for children in these areas.

questions.question: At what speed should you always drive?

options.text: At the same speed as other vehicles.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed depends on the road, weather, and legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when you cannot see clearly. High beams reflect light back at you in fog, making it harder to see. Low beams help other drivers see you without reducing your visibility.

questions.question: If your wheels go off the edge of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and carefully get back on the road when it is safe.
Turn back onto the road right away.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully get back on the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not try to turn back on the road immediately if your wheels drop off. Instead, slow down, check traffic, and gradually turn back when it is safe.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Stopping too much.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. Your tires lose grip and the car slides on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close behind other vehicles to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill on slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. Also, stay farther behind other vehicles than normal and avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes to slow down or stop unless your car has antilock brakes.

questions.question: What is the main way defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no mercy and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to handle them safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves and you should slow down.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what. Always give the right-of-way to all pedestrians, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking facing downhill on a road with or without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center of the road so your car will roll into the curb.

questions.question: A driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing at an intersection with no traffic light. Who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must give the right-of-way to pedestrians at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. At what speed can your car hydroplane?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away. As you go faster than 35 mph, tires cannot move the water as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under gates or barriers at a railroad crossing. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones may have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra caution to stay safe and protect other drivers and construction workers.

questions.question: Another driver is passing you in a no passing zone. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Passing zones are marked based on how far ahead drivers can see. Help the passing driver get back into your lane safely. This helps everyone avoid dangers ahead.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could make it unsafe. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
Fix the problem when you have the money.
Drive slower than normal.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any problem that could affect your vehicle's safety right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the problem is fixed.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a busy intersection. Other cars block your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may move in the direction shown if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop completely before moving in that direction.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the road tells drivers in that lane they must move in the direction shown. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When your vehicle will not completely clear the tracks on the other side.
When the crossing is in a city or town with lots of train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle will not completely clear the tracks on the other side.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time from either direction. Make sure your entire vehicle clears the tracks before you stop. Do not stop on the tracks.
